newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada raising tobacco taxes in small province.
newsitem.headline: Canada raising tobacco taxes in small province.

text.p: Canadian Finance Minister Paul Martin on Wednesday announced an increase in tobacco taxes in Prince Edward Island, supplementing identical increases announced earlier in four other provinces.
The federal excise tax will rise by C$0.70 per carton and the provincial tax by an identical amount, a Finance official said.

Prince Edward Island is Canada's smallest province. Martin had already secured agreement to raise taxes in Ontario, Quebec, Nova Scotia and New Brunswick as part of an overall government anti-tobacco strategy.
Canada's tobacco industry is about 65 percent-controlled by Imperial Tobacco Ltd, a unit of Imasco Ltd. Imasco is 40 percent-owned by Britain's B.A.T. Industries Plc .

Another big Canadian cigarette company is Rothmans, Benson and Hedges Inc, 60 percent-owned by Rothmans Inc -- a unit of Rothmans International Plc -- and 40 percent by Philip Morris Cos Inc. A third major player is RJR MacDonald, wholly owned by RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp unit R.J. Reynolds Tobacco International.
